page: Microsoft Azure D2a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DAv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 2 dedicated vCPUs, which map to 1 physical core and 2 threads. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per core) and includes 51 GB of local SSD storage. It does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a notable contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% with a stress-ng score of 2697.89, and Geekbench single-core performance is average at 1522.0. However, multi-core performance is weak, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 2697.89 (bottom 25%) and Geekbench multi-core scoring 1952.0 (bottom 10%). Memory performance is also a constraint; the passmark memory score of 1077.41 and small-block read-only memory bandwidth of 128.19 GB/sec both fall into the bottom 10%. Large-block read and write bandwidths are also weak, measuring 34.61 GB/sec and 24.14 GB/sec respectively.

Given these performance metrics, the D2a_v4 is appropriate for workloads that rely on single-threaded execution rather than parallel processing or high memory throughput. Single-threaded gzip compression (26.04 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (11.38 GB/sec) perform at average levels. Conversely, tasks requiring high concurrency or memory speed, such as database operations (Passmark database score of 952.03) and Redis SET operations (2.03 million operations/sec), perform poorly. This instance represents a low-resource, entry-level option within the AMD EPYC family, offering a cost-efficient profile for basic web serving, lightweight text processing, and development environments where multi-core scaling and high memory bandwidth are not critical.
